text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 1.94% today, continuing a strong two-week rally that has added 9% to the stock price. The move follows a significant dip in oil prices yesterday when Saudi Arabia signaled it would release more crude supplies after a pipeline attack, easing supply concerns that had been pushing crude higher. For a refiner like Marathon, lower oil prices directly improve profitability on the fuel they produce and sell — when the cost of their raw material (crude oil) drops while refined product prices hold relatively steady, their margins widen.

The broader context here is geopolitical stability and easing supply risk. News that the U.S. may be nearing an end to its conflict with Iran, combined with Saudi Arabia's willingness to boost exports, has reduced the premium investors were paying for oil due to Middle East tensions. At the same time, refineries are running at 96.8% capacity with healthy product inventories, meaning the industry is well-positioned to process crude and convert lower input costs into stronger earnings.
